Why Little Elm businesses miss calls

Little Elm sits on Lewisville Lake, with a lakefront district that draws weekend visitors. Over 12% of workers are in finance and real estate, and nearly 17% in professional services, while food and hospitality are close to 10%. Young families keep moving in, so homes, schools and clinics are all in demand. On warm weekends, local restaurants and marinas can get far more calls than their staff can handle.

Can you keep your Little Elm phone number?

Yes. Little Elm callers will usually see the 214, 469, 972 and 945 area codes, and you can keep the number customers already know. Everything is set up remotely, so you do not need new equipment or a visit to an office.

What to check before you go live

  1. Test real calls: ask awkward questions, not only easy ones, and listen to how it handles them.
  2. Set the rules: decide which calls transfer to a person and which become messages.
  3. Plan your minutes: estimate your busiest month, not an average one.
  4. Tell callers what you need to: Texas is generally treated as a one-party consent state for recording calls, but rules differ for callers in other states, so check with your advisor if you record calls.
